Name: Lo-debar
ModernLocation: Disputed; proposed sites include Tel Dover and Umm ed Debar
Description: The town in Gilead where Mephibosheth, Jonathan's lame son, lived in the house of Machir until David sent for him and restored Saul's land to him; Machir of Lo-debar later supplied David in his flight from Absalom.
BiblicalSignificance: Lo-debar is where David's kindness reached: a forgotten prince in an out-of-the-way town, brought to eat at the king's table continually.
RelatedPeople: Mephibosheth, Son of Jonathan; King David
